summary: Bhutan’s pledges combine conservation and forest restoration with broad agricultural transitions. It aims to maintain over 70% forest cover (a 2023 inventory figure of 69.71% is also reported), maintain 436 million tonnes of forest carbon stock outside protected areas, and place at least 50% of the land under protection. Climate-smart plantation and restoration cover 2,000 ha, equivalent to about 0.07% of the 30,348 km2 forest area mapped for 2022. Agricultural measures include 15 acres of agroforestry, an annual 5% shift from synthetic to organic fertilisers, improved practices on 14,971 ha, perennial-crop biomass expansion on 17,495 ha, and 200 ha/year of reduced continuous rice flooding. The two area-based farming targets equal roughly 14.6% and 17.1% of current mapped agriculture, respectively. Bhutan also targets 10,254 domestic biogas units and breed and feeding improvements for 8,333 dairy cattle.
